### State of the mathematical research

Write \(T=4\pi^2\) and let \(I^+(M)\) be the infimum of \(E_+\) over positive Yamabe classes on the fixed smooth homotopy sphere \(M\). A single such class with \(E_+\le T\) recognizes the standard smooth sphere, including the equality case by Chang–Gursky–Yang’s classification. The master asks first for the weaker **entry condition** \(I^+(M)<2T\). Constructing an initial class in this range on every smooth homotopy four-sphere remains open. genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn914717878view0","turn914717878view1"]}}

Once entry holds, take \(e_i=E_+(g_i)\to I^+(M)\). Suppose a marked cut gives two positive-Yamabe caps whose combined energy budget is below \(2T\). At least one cap is standard. On a hypothetical nonstandard \(M\), marked reassembly identifies the other cap with the original smooth type, giving
\[
m_{\mathrm{discarded}}\le e_i-I^+(M)+\gamma_{\mathrm{retained}},
\]
where \(\gamma_{\mathrm{retained}}\) is the net excess over the retained raw side. Thus a cut with vanishing costs and fixed positive chiral mass on **both entire sides** contradicts minimization. The manuscript derives the required caps from a short oriented annulus with uniform and strong \(W^{1,4}\) metric comparison and bounded full curvature on the splice. [Marked-cut argument](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/master/manuscript/marked_cut.tex) · [Short cut and local replacement](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/master/manuscript/variational_comparison.tex)

The second advance is that minimization itself forces strong local convergence of both chiral curvature densities on a supplied first-order marked comparison. The smooth limit is Bach-flat. Every smooth complete marked limit at a vanishing constant physical scale is flat, without assuming small Bach error on the source sequence. Consequently, when \(K_i=\max|\mathrm{Rm}_{g_i}|\to\infty\), every ball of radius \(A/\sqrt{K_i}\) loses its full curvature energy, uniformly in its center for fixed \(A\). The remaining possibilities include concentration on intervening scales, a closed nonround minimizer, and a round-base restart at the same energy. The positive-Ricci gauge locates smooth balls carrying almost all physical volume, but their complement can still carry the chiral energy. [Physical-scale results](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/master/manuscript/complete_limits.tex) · [Master research plan](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/master/research-plan/PLAN.md)

### Proposed next round

1. **Formalize the variational inequality first.** Reuse `geometricPositiveEnergies` to prove the one-sided repair bound \(\sum_jm_{ij}\le N_i(e_i-I^+(M))+\sum_j\gamma_{ij}\), then the two-sided nonsplitting inequality above. One concrete definition needs attention immediately. Route 03 uses a real `sInf` in the presence of an actual competitor. In Lean, `sInf (∅ : Set ℝ) = 0`, whereas the manuscript sets \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). I would carry an explicit positive-class witness through the first proofs and use an extended-valued infimum for universal entry statements. [Existing geometric energy definition](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/FirstOrderTwistor/GeometricCutDescent.lean)
2. **Extend Route 03 to the master’s short cut.** The current splice theorem already converts an \(L^2\) projection-error bound into the signed energy surcharge. Prove that bound for the actual interpolated metric, uniformly along the straightening path. Then use the zero-Yamabe energy wall on the joined manifold and transfer compactly supported tests to both caps. This gives a precise first geometric milestone without requiring an ALE compactification. [Existing splice theorem](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/FirstOrderTwistor/CapSplice.lean)
3. **Open one new investigation, `05_variational_comparison`.** Its main analytic target should be strong local chiral convergence and Bach stationarity from same-type replacement under \(C^0\cap W^{1,4}\) convergence and a local comparison-curvature bound. In parallel, formalize the physical quantile dichotomy and low-curvature annulus selection, keeping the attaining inner center and the entire median exterior. Producing a marked chart on that annulus remains a geometric research problem. The new working Ricci-scale draft supplies a further conditional target with scaled physical \(L^p\) Ricci control for \(p>2\). It was still outside the integrated master at the reviewed revision. [Physical Ricci-scale draft](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/master/manuscript/ricci_scales.tex)

### Why `FirstOrderTwistor` has so many files

Version 01 deliberately chose `FirstOrderTwistor` as the **shared Lean library for Routes 02–04**. The investigation folders own plans and proof records. The library holds their executable mathematics. It now contains **103 Lean source modules**. Its public entry point imports 58 directly and reaches the other 45 transitively. Of the 103, 45 have `Spin` names and seven have `Cylinder` names. There are genuine cross-route dependencies too: the spinor cover theorem imports the general energy-accounting theorem. [Public imports](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/FirstOrderTwistor.lean) · [Cross-route example](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/FirstOrderTwistor/SpinCoverAccounting.lean)

The historical name now understates the library’s scope. I would preserve its public imports, add a short route-to-module index, and put new master-specific code under a neutral `SmoothPoincare/` root with `Variational/` and `PhysicalScales/` subdirectories. That gives the new work a natural home without disrupting the checked dependency graph.
